column4: note
Parser.get(Class) twice / one OnceLock<SharedGrammar>::get_or_init twice (Arc::ptr_eq)
Parser.newInstance(Class) / share_grammar(build()) per call
Parser.get(Supplier) with one supplier instance / one OnceLock
two supplier lambdas building equal parsers / two OnceLock statics
Parser.getSupplier(Class) closures delegate to the class singleton / closures calling one accessor
a failing constructor is not cached: Java FactoryBoundCache stores only results; Rust sets the OnceLock only after Ok
ParserFactoryByClass.get(kind,Class): same key, other kind, no kind / one OnceLock per (grammar, kind) key
Java ClassAndKind(Class).kind() is Optional.empty (was Optional.of(null) -> NPE). Rust has no runtime node kind: the kind-less key is the plain factory row

a constructor taking Parsers(ItsOwnClass) re-enters the synchronized factory. Rust never recurses in OnceLock::get_or_init (reentrant init is unspecified); cycles use Rule(index), see lazy-construction-cycle
LazyChoice child Parser.get(Self) / Expr::Rule(own index), parse ((x))
getLazyParsers calls / OnceLock builder calls after three parses on the shared graph
one shared graph, three fresh contexts x! / y / x?
ParserNameContext with two distinct parsers named Item / RuleNames::new([.., Item, Item])
one parser under two parents is one entry (Java fixed in #845) / one rule referenced twice by Rule(index)
ParserNameContext.get / RuleNames::get for an undeclared name
Java default names are class names, so two WordParsers collide. Rust literals are unnamed; only Rule names enter RuleNames
ReferenceByNameParser resolves the first parser in flatten preorder (Item:a before Item:b), inputs a / b. Rust rejects the duplicate in RuleNames; the port chooses the first declaration explicitly
ReferenceByNameParser re-searches after a miss, so a parser named Late added after parse 1 is found / rebuilding rules re-resolves the name
ReferenceParser caches its miss for the instance lifetime / the Expr resolved once is kept when rules are extended
predicate evaluations during later parses in fresh contexts: Java caches the first lookup, Rust resolves at construction
Referencer.AbstractReference searches from the root on every call / a lookup function over the current rule vector
RuleNames::reference rejects an undeclared name at construction. Java has no strict lookup; its tolerant miss is the Missing alternative of cases.tsv (reference_or_never)
RuleNames::share rejects rules built out of the declared order. Java parsers carry their own names, so there is no index order to check
a shared singleton's parent is the last container constructed. Rust rules have no parent pointer; dynamic parents are RuleStack frames
findFirstToParent stops after 1000 parents. Rust has no parent walk; unbounded rule recursion is a resource_limit in both (left-recursion row)
A ::= A 'x' through a name reference: Java throws ParseLimitException ULX-PARSE-DEPTH-LIMIT (1024 active frames), Rust returns the non-recoverable rule-nesting resource_limit (256)
PseudoRootParser rejects setParent. In Rust any rule index can be the parse root
PseudoRootParser parses only a single child. Rust roots are one Expr::Rule(index)
AbstractPropagatableSource.getInvertMatchToChild before any parse / a fresh context's token_mode(); Rust keeps the mode per context, never on the shared graph
getInvertMatchFromParent without a source ancestor / token_mode().invert at the root
a leaf under NotPropagatableSource after parse / Custom parser under invert_match reading token_mode().invert
Parser.isTokenParsedBySpecifiedParser(token, exact class / superclass) / Node.rule == rule index / other index
ParsersSpecifier.contains by exact class / a set of rule indices
GrammarRule.nameOf: explicit, ItemParser class default, WordParser, null and blank overrides fall back to the class. Rust Rule.name is always explicit
ParserPrinter simple / detail / mostDetail over the parent path. Rust reports rule names through RuleStack
Name.of(fqcn) vs Name.of(Class); Name.classBaseOf vs Name.of(fqcn); Name.of(text) is interned. Rust rule names compare by text, so distinct Java kinds need distinct spellings
HasChildrenParser.newFiltered drops a direct child c, parse ab / Vec::retain on the sequence
newWithoutRecursive drops c at any depth keeping each combinator type (Java fixed in #845), parse ab / recursive Expr filter
ChildOccurs of WordParser / ConstructedSingleChildParser / Chain. Rust arity is the Expr variant
